_meta.purpose: Curated evidence-family signals that cannot be read out of STIX. ATT&CK v20 describes techniques in terms of LOG SOURCES (detection telemetry); it does not state whether a technique leaves durable host state. That judgement is made here, once per technique FAMILY (top-level ID), so it stays small and reviewable instead of being hand-typed ~700 times.
_meta.application: A technique inherits its family's signals from its top-level ID. Sub-technique-specific corrections go in testability_overrides.json, not here.

signals.artifact_family: Executing this technique normally leaves persistent on-disk / registry / config state that a current-state scan can read.
signals.memory_family: Primary evidence is volatile process memory; a retrospective disk+log scan cannot recover it.
signals.network_family: Primary evidence is network traffic; requires a network sensor, not a host scan.

_meta.review_note: Every entry carries a reason. An entry asserting artifact_family is a claim that irscan could in principle find something, so it must name the artifact. Families absent from this file contribute no signal and fall through to log-source-derived classification.

artifact_family.T1037: Logon/boot initialisation script files on disk, plus HKCU UserInitMprLogonScript registry values and /etc/rc* script contents.
artifact_family.T1053: Scheduled job definitions persist: Windows Task Scheduler XML under System32\Tasks plus registry TaskCache, at job files, crontab files, systemd timer units.
artifact_family.T1078: Local account objects and their group memberships persist in SAM / /etc/passwd and remain enumerable as current state.
artifact_family.T1098: Account and group-membership changes persist, as do ~/.ssh/authorized_keys entries.
artifact_family.T1112: Registry values are current state by definition; the modified value is the artifact.
artifact_family.T1133: Remote-access service configuration persists (sshd_config, RDP registry settings, VPN client config).
artifact_family.T1136: A created account persists as an enumerable account object.
artifact_family.T1137: Office persistence lives in template files, add-in manifests and Office registry keys on disk.
artifact_family.T1176: Browser and IDE extensions persist as unpacked directories and manifest files.
artifact_family.T1197: BITS job queue state persists in the qmgr database until the job completes or expires.
artifact_family.T1505: Server software components persist as files: web shells, IIS modules, SQL stored procedures, transport agents.
artifact_family.T1542: Pre-OS boot persistence lives in the bootloader, EFI system partition or device firmware.
artifact_family.T1543: Service and daemon definitions persist: Windows service registry keys and binaries, systemd unit files.
artifact_family.T1546: Event-triggered execution persists in WMI event subscriptions, registry trigger keys, shell profile files and udev rules.
artifact_family.T1547: Autostart entries persist: Run keys, Startup folder shortcuts, kernel module files, XDG autostart .desktop files.
artifact_family.T1554: The modified or backdoored binary itself is the artifact and remains on disk.
artifact_family.T1556: Authentication-process modifications persist: PAM configuration, password filter DLL registration, SSP registration, network provider DLLs.
artifact_family.T1574: Hijacked execution flow leaves planted DLLs/shared objects, altered search paths, and LD_PRELOAD / ld.so.preload entries.
artifact_family.T1027: Obfuscated or packed payload files remain on disk and are inspectable as current state.
artifact_family.T1036: Masquerading is expressed in durable file metadata: name, path, extension, icon, signature mismatch.
artifact_family.T1564: Hidden artifacts persist: hidden files and directories, NTFS alternate data streams, hidden accounts, hidden windows registry entries.
artifact_family.T1553: Trust subversion persists in the root certificate store, SIP/trust-provider registry registration, and code-signing policy configuration.
artifact_family.T1552: Unsecured credentials persist in files, registry values, shell history files, private key files and Group Policy Preferences XML.
artifact_family.T1555: Password stores persist as credential vault files and browser credential databases on disk.
artifact_family.T1222: File and directory permission changes are current state: ACLs and POSIX modes are directly readable.
artifact_family.T1685: Defence impairment persists as configuration state: disabled services, AV exclusion lists, audit policy, event log channel settings, auditd rules.
artifact_family.T1686: Firewall impairment persists as firewall profile/rule configuration state.
artifact_family.T1690: History-logging suppression persists in shell configuration (HISTFILE/HISTSIZE settings, PowerShell transcription settings).
artifact_family.T1070: Partial: log clearing leaves its own traces (a near-empty channel, Security 1102, gaps, and absent history files) even though the removed content is gone.
artifact_family.T1205: Traffic signalling persists as installed socket filters, iptables/nftables rules and port-knock daemon configuration.
artifact_family.T1547.006: Loaded kernel modules and their on-disk .ko files persist.
artifact_family.T1484: Group Policy and trust modifications persist as GPO files in SYSVOL and as domain trust objects.
artifact_family.T1653: Power setting changes persist in registry / systemd-logind configuration.
artifact_family.T1668: Exclusive-control mechanisms persist as mutexes/lock files and the configuration that created them.
artifact_family.T1558.005: Kerberos credential cache files persist on disk under /tmp or a configured ccache path.
artifact_family.T1207: Rogue domain controller registration persists in directory objects and local service/registry state.
artifact_family.T1649: Stolen or forged authentication certificates persist in certificate stores and as exported key/cert files.
artifact_family.T1539: Stolen session cookies originate from browser cookie databases that persist on disk.
artifact_family.T1003: Partial: credential dumping itself is largely telemetry, but dump output files, registry hive copies and shadow-copy exports persist on disk.

memory_family.T1055: Process injection leaves its evidence in the memory of the target process; after reboot or process exit nothing durable remains.
memory_family.T1620: Reflective code loading never writes the loaded image to disk.
memory_family.T1056: Input capture hooks live in process memory; only the capture output file, if any, is durable.
memory_family.T1003.001: LSASS memory is the evidence; irscan must never read it. Only a dump file left on disk is durable.
memory_family.T1497: Sandbox/VM evasion decisions happen in memory at runtime.
memory_family.T1622: Debugger evasion is a runtime control-flow decision.
memory_family.T1211: Exploitation for defence evasion is a runtime memory-corruption event.

network_family.T1040: Network sniffing is observed on the wire or by a promiscuous-mode indicator, not by durable host state.
network_family.T1557: Adversary-in-the-middle is a traffic-level phenomenon requiring network visibility.
network_family.T1187: Forced authentication is an outbound authentication attempt visible in network or off-host authentication logs.
network_family.T1102: Web service C2 is network traffic.
network_family.T1041: Exfiltration over the C2 channel is network traffic.
network_family.T1048: Exfiltration over an alternative protocol is network traffic.
network_family.T1029: Scheduled transfer is a traffic-timing pattern.
network_family.T1030: Data transfer size limits are a traffic pattern.
network_family.T1105: Ingress tool transfer is network traffic, though a transferred file may persist on disk.
network_family.T1046: Network service discovery is observed as scanning traffic.
